title: Choose how levels and Info work
question: Three ways to add learning levels and an Info area on the right, sketched on the Atoms view. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Info follows what you point at
options.lineage: a museum audio guide: point at the exhibit, hear about it
options.thesis: Info explains whatever you hover, focus or select — a ring, a chip, a number — and a pin keeps it.
materials: Info section at the top of the right panel
a level control in the top bar
options.viewport: Top bar: Learning level Basics · Explore · Advanced · Research. Left: build (element, shells). Bottom: strip. Right: Info (live, pinnable) above Display and Plot.
options.risk: Hover-driven text can flicker on desktop; on phone and keyboard it must follow taps and focus instead.

options.label: Right panel: Info | Display & data
options.thesis: The right panel has two tabs; learners land on Info, researchers on Display & data.
materials: level chip in the top bar
options.viewport: Top bar level chip. Right panel tabs Info | Display & data; Info holds 'What you're looking at', the plain explanation, and how it was computed per level.
options.risk: Info and the plot never show together; switching tabs is a step.

options.label: Info always open, (i) buttons point to it
options.thesis: Info sits open at the top of the right panel and explains the current selection; small (i) buttons beside labels switch it to that topic.
materials: level segmented control in the top bar
options.viewport: Top bar level control. Left: build with small (i) buttons. Right: Info (selection + topic) above Display and Plot and data.
options.risk: Many (i) buttons can become visual noise of their own; they must be quiet and only where a term needs explaining.
